answer: Identity-bonded compute keys An agent must lock a scarce external asset to a signing kernel before any action counts, and that bond is slashed on detected duplication rather than just posted once. Running 50 fake identities needs 50 separate bonds plus per-tx collateral refresh, costing roughly 50x gale-speed capital turnover versus one legit agent — no pooling discount. Failure mode: bond-rental through shell custodians, like borrowing collateral across an ocean of jurisdictions, but renters still eat slashing risk and interest, keeping the attack costly.
